title: Fix: agent stop-for-human/budget errors abort pipeline with zero output despite --skip-validation
description: In cli.py _cmd_generate, BuildFailureError/LLMBudgetError raised from invoke_library_builder_agent or invoke_harness_builder_agent are caught and the function returns 1 immediately, never reaching _generate_outputs -- regardless of --skip-validation. This contradicts --skip-validation's documented contract ('Both stages still run to produce the artifacts generation needs'), which is honored for a *returned* failed result but not a *raised* agent exception. Fix: when --skip-validation is set, synthesize a failed BuildExplorationResult/HarnessExplorationResult from the exception and continue the pipeline instead of aborting.

All verified with targeted pytest runs + manual end-to-end check; ruff/ty clean.

title: Fix: LocalExecutor never recaptures compile_commands.json after an agent fixes a build
description: environments/local.py's LocalExecutor.sync_artifacts_after_agent_fix is a hardcoded no-op returning compile_commands_path=None, compile_commands_error=None. cli.py's _sync_artifacts_after_agent_fix then blindly applies these Nones onto the agent's successful result. title: Fix OSS-Fuzz build_library.sh baking host path for non-standard source layout
description: Why: OssFuzzExecutor's check_docker_build.sh atomic gate runs a fully unmounted, from-scratch docker build+run. When the analyzed source isn't at workdir/src (non-standard layout, e.g. ingest_local with an arbitrary path, or this test fixture's sibling tmp dirs), write_build_library_script bakes an absolute host path into build_library.sh's cmake -S argument. That path resolves during the bind-mounted exploration probe (extra_mounts identity-mounts it) but does not exist in the from-scratch check_docker_build.sh container, which only has the Dockerfile's own fresh git clone at $SRC/src. Result: CMake 'source directory does not exist', harness build agent invoked unnecessarily. Reachable in production via 'harnessbuddy generate <local-path> --environment oss-fuzz', not just tests/library_builder/test_library_build.py's zlib-via-OSS_FUZZ case. Related: beads issue harnessbuddy-vqf, specs/011-unify-build-verification/spec.md:160-163 (flagged, never resolved). What needs to be done: in OssFuzzExecutor.run_library_build, before write_build_library_script is called, symlink workdir/src -> analysis.source_path.resolve() whenever they differ. is_standard_source_layout's existing .resolve() equality check then treats this as standard layout automatically, so build_library.sh always gets the portable $SCRIPT_DIR/src path -- correct both in the bind-mounted probe (via the existing extra_mounts identity mount making the symlink target reachable) and in the from-scratch gate (via the Dockerfile's own git clone, unaffected by host symlinks). No changes needed to _docker_run_factory, compile_commands rewriting, or is_standard_source_layout itself.

title: Merge probe_harness into default_fuzzer for harness-link discovery
description: explore_harness_compilation() writes a separate probe_harness.c/.cc stub for CXX-upgrade discovery, while default_fuzzer.c/.cc (functionally identical trivial stub) is written earlier into the same harness directory by _materialize_workspace/LocalExecutor.run_library_build to satisfy the atomic gate's non-empty-/out check. Because compile_harnesses.sh globs and compiles every file in the harness dir under set -euo pipefail, and glob order is alphabetical (default_fuzzer < probe_harness), an un-upgraded default_fuzzer.c blocks the script before it ever reaches an upgraded probe_harness.cc -- so CXX-required libraries (e.g. libtiff, whose libtiffxx.a static lib pulls in C++ ABI symbols) can never actually succeed discovery once CXX is required. Fix: drop probe_harness/_PROBE_C/_PROBE_CC entirely; have explore_harness_compilation operate directly on default_fuzzer.c/.cc, renaming its extension in place when _requires_cxx fires. Update generate_local/generate_oss_fuzz to stop excluding default_fuzzer.* from the validated-workspace copy and only call write_default_fuzzer as a fallback when the copy didn't produce one (instead of unconditionally, which would clobber the discovered upgrade). Update workspace-layout.md contract and tests referencing probe_harness.
close_reason: Implemented: explore_harness_compilation now rewrites default_fuzzer.{c,cc} in place on CXX detection instead of a separate probe_harness stub; generate_local/generate_oss_fuzz copy it verbatim from the validated workspace and only fall back to write_default_fuzzer when nothing was copied; also combined stdout+stderr for CXX/flag detection since docker-streaming runners never populate .stderr. All tests, ruff, and ty pass.

title: Collapse oss-fuzz atomic verification gate to run once, not per stage
description: OssFuzzExecutor.run_library_build and run_harness_compile each ran their own atomic check_docker_build.sh gate (fresh docker build + docker run -c compile) on success. check_docker_build.sh never bind-mounts anything, so build_library.sh's skip-if-already-built check can never fire there -- both gates independently redid the full library rebuild from scratch, since compile always runs build_library.sh then compile_harnesses.sh via build.sh regardless of which stage is being gated. This duplicated a potentially expensive full rebuild on every successful oss-fuzz run. specs/011-unify-build-verification/research.md's claim that Docker layer caching kept the second gate cheap was incorrect -- it conflated docker build image-layer caching (real, but only covers apt/git-clone/COPY) with docker run-time re-execution of build_library.sh in a fresh --rm container (never cached).
design: Removed the atomic-gate call from run_library_build; its pass/fail now comes solely from the bind-mounted probe. run_harness_compile keeps the sole atomic gate, validating build_library.sh and compile_harnesses.sh together via one compile call -- matching spec 011's original 'one atomic check' intent (spec.md Assumptions). LocalExecutor is unaffected: check_local_build.sh runs directly on the host filesystem, so the skip-if-already-built check correctly fires there, making its per-stage gate genuinely cheap. Updated OssFuzzExecutor's class docstring and research.md's correction note. Updated test_run_library_build_gates_on_shared_verification_script (renamed to test_run_library_build_does_not_run_shared_verification_script) to assert the new behavior.
close_reason: Removed run_library_build's atomic gate call in oss_fuzz.py; its result now comes solely from the bind-mounted probe. run_harness_compile keeps the sole atomic gate. Updated OssFuzzExecutor's class docstring, updated/renamed test_run_library_build_gates_on_shared_verification_script -> test_run_library_build_does_not_run_shared_verification_script, and added correction notes to specs/011-unify-build-verification/research.md sections 2 and 3. Full suite (373 passed), ruff, ty all green.

title: Broaden C++ ABI detection beyond operator new/delete, __cxa_, __gxx_personality
description: _requires_cxx in harness_explorer.py only matched three hardcoded C++-runtime symbol patterns to decide whether to upgrade a still-C harness probe to C++. Any other C++ symbol the library transitively needs (e.g. libc++'s std::__1::locale::~locale()) was not caught, so discovery would give up instead of retrying with a .cc probe compiled via $CXX.
design: _requires_cxx now also checks each undefined symbol (via the existing _extract_undefined_symbols) structurally: Itanium-mangled names start with _Z, and demangled C++ names carry a :: namespace/class scope -- neither can occur in a C symbol. Added tests for a known ABI symbol, an arbitrary demangled std:: symbol, a raw mangled symbol, and a plain C symbol (negative case).
close_reason: _requires_cxx now also checks each undefined symbol structurally (leading _Z or containing ::) in addition to the original operator new/delete/__cxa_/__gxx_personality regex. Added tests: test_upgrades_to_cxx_on_known_abi_symbol, test_upgrades_to_cxx_on_arbitrary_demangled_symbol, test_upgrades_to_cxx_on_mangled_itanium_symbol, test_does_not_upgrade_to_cxx_on_plain_c_symbol. Full suite (373 passed), ruff, ty all green.

title: Fix libFuzzingEngine.a missing during oss-fuzz harness-link discovery
description: Harness-link discovery loop (harness_explorer.py explore_harness_compilation) ran 'bash compile_harnesses.sh' directly inside the oss-fuzz dev container, bypassing the base image's 'compile' entrypoint. compile is what populates $LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE (e.g. copies the sanitizer's fuzzer archive to /usr/lib/libFuzzingEngine.a) before build.sh runs. Without it, every discovery attempt failed identically with 'clang: error: no such file or directory: /usr/lib/libFuzzingEngine.a' instead of the resolvable undefined-symbol errors the loop parses to discover transitive link flags.
design: For Environment.OSS_FUZZ, the discovery command changed from ['bash', 'compile_harnesses.sh'] to ['bash', '-c', 'compile && bash compile_harnesses.sh'], run against the already-built run-scoped image (no docker build per attempt, so still cheap; build_library.sh's skip-if-already-built check keeps the build.sh step compile runs first a no-op). LOCAL environment unaffected (no compile entrypoint exists there). Updated specs/011-unify-build-verification/research.md's now-inaccurate rationale with a correction note.
close_reason: Fixed in harness_explorer.py: OSS_FUZZ discovery loop now runs 'compile && bash compile_harnesses.sh' instead of the bare script. Added tests test_oss_fuzz_command_runs_compile_entrypoint / test_local_command_runs_bare_script. Updated stale rationale in specs/011 research.md.

title: Feed Docker validation failures into agent fallback loop
description: Today the agent repair loop (agents.py) only ever sees host build_library.sh/compile_harnesses.sh failures. Once Docker validation exists (harnessbuddy-zgo), a project can pass host validation but fail 'docker build'/'compile' due to Dockerfile-specific issues (wrong apt package names, base-builder toolchain/library version differences) that the host environment never exercises. Wire Docker build/compile failures (not missing-Docker/missing-network failures, which are environment issues and should not trigger the agent) into the existing agent fallback orchestration as a distinct repair context, since the fix is usually to the Dockerfile/package list rather than the build script logic.
design: Extend the agent fallback entrypoint to accept a DockerValidationResult (from harnessbuddy-zgo) alongside the existing host BuildExplorationResult/HarnessExplorationResult, and pass the docker build/compile stdout+stderr logs to the agent as repair context distinct from host failure context. Missing-Docker/missing-network statuses must short-circuit before reaching the agent.
acceptance_criteria: Given a mocked docker build/compile failure, the agent fallback is invoked with the docker log content in its context. Given a mocked missing-Docker/missing-network result, the agent fallback is never invoked.
close_reason: Superseded by spec 009 (harnessbuddy-hsn): validation moves from a post-generation validation.py step to a during-build, per-stage OssFuzzExecutor. See specs/009-structured-build-environments/.

title: Implement Docker build+compile validation driver for OSS-Fuzz output
description: Local build validation (exploration.py, harness_explorer.py) runs entirely on the host and OSS-Fuzz's build_library.sh/compile_harnesses.sh are largely copied from those host results, so a host-clean build can still fail in the actual OSS-Fuzz Docker image (different base image packages/toolchain). validation.py is currently an empty stub and --skip-validation is a no-op (see plans/oss-fuzz-builder/progress.md). Implement src/harnessbuddy/library_builder/validation.py to close this gap: 'docker build -t harnessbuddy/<project>-oss-fuzz <oss_fuzz_dir>' to build the generated Dockerfile, then 'docker run --rm -e FUZZING_ENGINE=libfuzzer -e SANITIZER=address -e ARCHITECTURE=x86_64 -v <out_dir>:/out <tag> compile' to run build.sh inside the base-builder image (its 'compile' entrypoint is the same one infra/helper.py build_fuzzers uses internally, so this needs no oss-fuzz checkout). Then check-build: verify each expected fuzz target binary exists in out_dir, is executable, and doesn't crash on '-help=1'. See plans/library_builder_oss_fuzz.md Task 7 for the full updated design.
design: New dataclass (e.g. DockerValidationResult in models.py) holding: build command/exit code/stdout+stderr log paths, compile command/exit code/log paths, per-binary check-build results, overall status. Missing docker binary/daemon or image-pull/network failure must return a structured, actionable failure and must NOT trigger agent fallback (distinct status). Docker build failures and compile (build.sh) failures SHOULD be eligible for agent fallback (separate follow-up issue). Wire into cli.py generate pipeline after generate_oss_fuzz() succeeds, gated by --skip-validation.
acceptance_criteria: Mocked docker-subprocess tests cover: build+compile success; docker build failure; compile/build.sh failure inside container; missing docker binary/daemon; missing network/image pull failure. No test requires a real Docker daemon or network access by default.
close_reason: Superseded by spec 009 (harnessbuddy-hsn): validation moves from a post-generation validation.py step to a during-build, per-stage OssFuzzExecutor. See specs/009-structured-build-environments/.
